raw_text_presence.scope: Persisted analytics graph nodes, edges, partition statistics, and algorithm metrics do not carry raw message text.
raw_text_presence.basis: Graph construction stores opaque graph identities, direction, character counts, affect, engagement, topic/entity signals, temporal relationships, and aggregate graph metrics rather than source text.

message.basis: Message graph node IDs are deterministically derived from account-scoped opaque message references.

conversation.basis: Conversation graph node IDs are deterministically derived from account-scoped opaque conversation references.

participant.basis: Creator and counterpart participant nodes are stable graph identities derived from opaque participant/account references.

canonical_joinability.basis: A party that already knows the canonical account/conversation/participant/message identifiers can deterministically recompute the domain-separated opaque references and graph identities used by the analytics plane.

unique_participant_semantics.basis: Participant nodes retain role and relationship structure across conversations/messages, with linked affect, engagement, topic/entity, timing, response, and graph-algorithm semantics.

inference_or_reconstruction_capability.basis: The graph cannot reproduce message wording, but preserves message-level and participant-level behavioral/semantic relationships that can reveal properties of the source interactions.

usefulness_after_identifier_removal.basis: Aggregate topology and some semantic distributions can remain analytically useful, but removing stable account/participant/conversation/message linkage materially degrades relationship, chronology, drill-down, and longitudinal interpretation.

classification_limitations: This classification addresses application-level persisted graph content; it does not claim anonymization or make a Legal retention determination.
Raw-text absence does not imply absence of personal or identifying semantic information.

raw_text_presence.scope: Persisted analytics projection documents contain enrichments, metrics, opaque references, provenance, and graph summary rather than raw message text.
raw_text_presence.basis: AnalyticsProjection persists MessageEnrichment, ConversationMetrics, CreatorMetrics, analyzer provenance, window/projection metadata, and graph summary; MessageEnrichment carries semantic outputs and opaque refs but no text field.

message.basis: MessageEnrichment stores an account-scoped deterministic message_ref.

conversation.basis: MessageEnrichment and ConversationMetrics store deterministic conversation_ref values.

participant.basis: MessageEnrichment and ConversationMetrics store deterministic participant_ref values.

canonical_joinability.basis: Opaque analytics refs are domain-separated SHA-256 references deterministically computed from known canonical identifiers; they do not embed plaintext source IDs but remain recomputable by the product from those IDs.

unique_participant_semantics.basis: Per-participant conversation metrics and per-message enrichments preserve sentiment, topics/entities, engagement, response behavior, counts, timing, and longitudinal semantics under stable opaque references.

inference_or_reconstruction_capability.basis: The persisted projection does not contain raw text, but its per-message and per-participant semantic outputs can strongly reveal characteristics of the underlying conversations.

usefulness_after_identifier_removal.basis: Creator-level aggregates and some aggregate distributions remain useful, while stripping message/conversation/participant refs removes drill-down, participant-specific, conversation-specific, and longitudinal capabilities.

classification_limitations: This classification does not establish that every future analyzer produces the same semantic fields; it classifies the closed persisted AnalyticsProjection contract at the pinned baseline.
Opaque deterministic references are pseudonymous linkage keys, not anonymous identifiers.

raw_text_presence.scope: Projection-store identity, publication epochs, and generation lifecycle rows contain coordination metadata rather than message content.
raw_text_presence.basis: The persisted fields are store/generation IDs, account partition ref, revisions/digests, publication/ownership/lease state, and validation/activation timestamps.

message.basis: No message-level reference is part of the projection-generation state contract.

conversation.basis: No conversation-level reference is part of the projection-generation state contract.

participant.basis: No participant-level reference is part of the projection-generation state contract.

canonical_joinability.basis: Generation rows retain the opaque creator-account partition and canonical revision/content digests, but no per-message, per-conversation, or per-participant linkage.

unique_participant_semantics.basis: The object is projection coordination state and does not persist participant-specific analytics semantics.

inference_or_reconstruction_capability.basis: Generation/revision/digest metadata can establish that a projection existed but does not itself reconstruct message content or participant analytics.

usefulness_after_identifier_removal.basis: Without account/generation linkage the remaining lifecycle metadata does not provide a meaningful conversational analytics capability.

classification_limitations: Canonical content digests can act as equality/freshness evidence and should not be treated as semantically empty merely because they do not expose source text.

raw_text_presence.scope: The aggregate object mixes several tables. conversation_summaries.document_json copies the latest message text, while projection_message_analysis and LPG material do not generally store the raw corpus.
raw_text_presence.basis: ProjectionRepository._write_conversation_summaries writes latest_message.text from projection_messages into conversation_summaries.document_json.

message.basis: projection_message_analysis and LPG message material retain message_id/entity_id; conversation_summaries also retain latest_message.message_id.

conversation.basis: The constituent rows and summary documents retain creator_account_id plus conversation_id.

participant.basis: conversation_summaries.document_json contains platform_user_id/display_name and LPG conversation documents persist platform_user_id/display_name.

canonical_joinability.basis: The Bridge read model retains creator account, conversation, message, and participant identifiers that can be joined directly to canonical rows within the same installation.

unique_participant_semantics.basis: The object retains participant identity/display information plus conversation summaries, latest-message content, per-message analysis, sentiment, and linked conversation/message graph structure.

inference_or_reconstruction_capability.basis: conversation_summaries can reproduce the latest copied message text for a conversation, while the remaining analysis/LPG material retains additional source-linked semantic information without reproducing the full raw history.

usefulness_after_identifier_removal.basis: Some aggregate/semantic documents remain interpretable, but removing account/conversation/message/participant linkage substantially degrades paging, drill-down, relationship, attribution, and longitudinal capabilities.

classification_limitations: Raw-text reconstruction is limited to the subset copied into summary documents; this classification does not claim the object can reconstruct the entire deleted message corpus.
The canonical registry now records this PRESENT_SUBSET fact; no Legal-policy conclusion is selected by that correction.

raw_text_presence.scope: projection_messages persists the full text field for each projected message row.
raw_text_presence.basis: The projection_messages schema defines text TEXT NOT NULL alongside message_id, conversation_id, sent_at, direction, and sentiment.

message.basis: message_id is a first-class projection_messages key.

conversation.basis: conversation_id is persisted with each projection message.

participant.basis: projection_messages does not contain sender/participant identifiers; participant attribution can remain available through related conversation/derived objects.

canonical_joinability.basis: creator_account_id, conversation_id, and message_id are directly compatible with the canonical account/message identity domain.

unique_participant_semantics.basis: Raw message content, conversation linkage, direction, timestamp, and sentiment preserve source-specific conversational semantics even though participant ID is not stored in this table.

inference_or_reconstruction_capability.basis: The object is a direct persisted copy of message text and associated message/conversation identity and timing metadata.

usefulness_after_identifier_removal.basis: Text remains analytically meaningful without message/conversation IDs, but paging, source attribution, chronology across conversations, and durable joins are materially degraded.

classification_limitations: Participant linkage is absent from projection_messages itself but may be recoverable from other surviving Bridge objects, so this row must not be read in isolation when evaluating durable deletion.

raw_text_presence.scope: Projection generation/change/application coordination rows do not persist message text.
raw_text_presence.basis: projection_accounts, projection_change_log, and projection_work_applied store generation/revision/work metadata; projection_change_log can retain touched conversation identifiers.

message.basis: No message identifier is part of these coordination tables.

conversation.basis: projection_change_log.touched_conversations_json can retain direct conversation identifiers as serialized change metadata.

participant.basis: No participant identifier is part of the Bridge projection coordination-state schema.

canonical_joinability.basis: creator_account_id and serialized touched conversation IDs can join directly to canonical identity domains, while generation/read/work identifiers are projection coordination identities.

unique_participant_semantics.basis: The object records projection coordination and touched-conversation metadata rather than participant-specific content or analytics.

inference_or_reconstruction_capability.basis: The state can reveal that particular conversations changed and which generations/work were applied, but it cannot itself reproduce message content or participant analytics.

usefulness_after_identifier_removal.basis: After account/conversation/generation/work identity is removed, the remaining coordination metadata does not provide meaningful conversational analytics.

classification_limitations: Conversation-touch metadata is still linkable operational data even though this object is classified as coordination-only for semantic inference.
